title: Essay v4: have we found a way for Harbour to tidy as it works?
description:
Write an essay answering one question: have we found a way for Harbour to tidy the codebase as it works?

Our answer is positive, with plenty of room to improve. Say that plainly up front. Then tell the true story of what we've learned: what the loop was, what happened when a move was finished versus only started, how our first measure was overturned, and what we noticed about ourselves along the way. End with why this is exciting and where it can go next. The paths ahead are many and varied. What makes us hopeful is that we now have a general way to keep improving, by stepping back and looking at the shape of the work, plus an awareness of our own habits and careful checks against them. The essay is a waypoint, not a verdict.

Two things we learned this morning aren't written down anywhere yet. First, each hand-off between agents tends to lose the original intent and gain detail, like a photocopy of a photocopy. Second, whenever something went wrong, we kept adding rules to the briefs instead of consolidating them. That's the same habit we were trying to stop in the code: adding beside instead of finishing. We pushed Harbour off its default of moving straight on to the next ticket, and we felt that friction in ourselves. The friction is a sign it's working. Plain briefs, which every step reads directly, are the next thing we'll try. Treat all of this as observation, not result.

The heart of it is a picture of two pipelines. In the old one, tickets ran in a line and each agent finished its own task and left, so copies and leftovers built up between tasks and no one's job was to clear them. In the new one, there is a look before the work, a decision on how big the move should be, the change itself, and then a tidy of whatever the change left behind. Show why the first built up mess, and how the second counteracts it and leaves the code tidier. Explain the improvements at that level: how each one is meant to work, the idea behind it, and the reason for it. Where a reader would expect a plain description, give one, not a task ID, and stay out of the details of Harbour's internals. Keep the spirit of the earlier versions and of the data: the story we have been telling, and the result we actually found.

Unlike the papers, the essay is for people like John Kershaw, who builds Harbour, to read: people who care about this work but weren't inside it. Make it interesting and easy to read, with a sensible structure. Tell it with visuals and metaphors, so a reader gets a true sense of what's happening, what we learned, why it's exciting and where it goes next. Use plain words and no internal jargon. The earlier versions use images that weren't understood: a forcefield held by a hand, a trig point, a ball that binds, the Towers of Hanoi, film versus stills. Leave them out unless you can say them plainly.

The facts are in the paper (`docs/papers/harbour/cleaner-than-it-started.md`), the earlier versions of this essay, and the notebook in `docs/plans/survey/`. Take numbers from the paper and claim nothing it doesn't. Use the essay format in `docs/papers/standard.md`. Aim for around 2,000 words. Write it as version 4 of `docs/papers/harbour/the-place-became-somebodys-job.md`, with a better title.

When it's written, have a fresh reader without our context read it and tell you where they got lost, and fix what helps. Open a pull request but don't merge it: John reads it first.

comments.body: Essay v4, *Clearing up as it goes*, is up for review: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2343 (commit bd1181ab, branch `lin-4340-essay-v4`). It answers yes up front, with plenty of room to improve, and is told through two pipelines: the old line, and look first → decide the size → change → tidy what it left. The two observations from 7 November are included and marked as observations. A fresh reader went through it, and the fixes are listed in the PR. Unit tests pass locally. Not merged: John reads it first.
Merged on John's go-ahead: PR #2343, squash `e63c2f69` at head `bd1181ab`, all CI checks green. Written by one writer on `opus` from the plain brief; John reads it in the Library.
